ArtifactMeta.description:
Metadata for a generated, content-addressed PNG artifact.

This struct captures the identity, generation parameters, and
storage location of a single output artifact produced by a worker.
The `hash` field is the SHA-256 hex content address used by
`anvilml-artifacts` as its primary key.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the artifact was created.

file_path.description: Filesystem path to the saved PNG file.

hash.description: SHA-256 hex content address — primary key for artifact storage.

job_id.description: UUID of the job that produced this artifact.

seed.description: Random seed used for generation (i64 to support negative seeds).

steps.description: Number of diffusion steps used in generation.

BulkClearParams.description:
HTTP query parameters for `DELETE /v1/jobs` (bulk clear endpoint).

The `status` parameter selects which terminal jobs to remove:
- `completed` — only Completed jobs
- `failed` — only Failed jobs
- `cancelled` — only Cancelled jobs
- `all` — all terminal jobs (Completed + Failed + Cancelled)

Returns `400 Bad Request` for any unrecognized value.

status.description: Filter by job status. Must be one of: completed, failed, cancelled, all.

CapabilitySource.description:
Where an `InferenceCaps` value came from.

`PyTorch` is the only source an arch module's loader is permitted to make a
compute-dtype decision from at runtime. `DeviceTable` and `Fallback` are
pre-spawn hints for scheduling estimates only.

ComponentVersions.description:
Per-component version report returned by `GET /v1/system/versions`.

Fields:
- `anvilml_version`: compile-time crate version from `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`.
- `rust_version`: runtime `rustc` SemVer from `rustc_version_runtime::version()`.
- `python_version`: from `AppState.env_report`, `None` if not yet collected.
- `torch_version`: from `AppState.env_report`, `None` if not yet collected.

anvilml_version.description: AnvilML crate version, resolved at compile time.

python_version.description:
Python interpreter version string, or `None` if the worker has not
yet reported it.

rust_version.description: Rust compiler version, resolved at runtime via `rustc_version_runtime`.

torch_version.description:
PyTorch version string, or `None` if the import failed or torch
is not installed.

DeviceType.description: The compute backend or execution target of a device.

EnumerationSource.description: Where a device was enumerated from.

EnvReport.description:
Python runtime environment report collected at worker startup preflight.

The scheduler uses this to verify the worker's Python and PyTorch
environment, provisioning status, and the node types it supports.

node_types.description: The node types registered by this worker, reported at startup.

preflight_ok.description: Whether all preflight checks passed (interpreter exists, Python version OK, torch importable).

provisioning.description: The provisioning status of the worker's environment.

python_path.description: Path to the Python interpreter used by the worker (e.g. `./worker/.venv/bin/python3`).

python_version.description: The Python interpreter version string (e.g. `"3.12.3"`), or `None` if unavailable.

reason.description: An optional human-readable reason when `preflight_ok` is `false`.

torch_version.description:
The PyTorch version string if `import torch` succeeded, or `None` if
the import failed or torch is not installed.

GpuDevice.description: A single detected compute device (GPU or CPU).

arch.description: Architecture string (e.g. "Ada Lovelace", "RDNA 3"). None for CPU.

capabilities_source.description: Where the capability values came from.

caps.description: Per-device inference capabilities (bf16, fp16, fp8, etc.).

index.description: Zero-based device index as reported by the OS/driver.

vram_free_mib.description: Free VRAM in mebibytes at time of detection.

HardwareInfo.description:
Complete hardware snapshot: host info, all detected compute devices, and
the aggregate inference capabilities across all devices.

This is the primary output of hardware enumeration — produced once at server
startup and used by the scheduler for device selection and the worker
dispatcher for routing jobs.

gpus.description: All detected compute devices on the host.

inference_caps.description:
Aggregate inference capabilities across all detected devices.
Represents the intersection of per-device capabilities.

HealthResponse.description:
JSON response body for the `/health` liveness probe.

Per `ANVILML_DESIGN.md §13.4`: `200 { status, version, uptime_s }`.

uptime_s.description: Seconds of uptime, computed as `(Instant::now() - start_time).as_secs()`.

HostInfo.description: Minimal host information for the hardware snapshot.

hostname.description: The hostname of the machine as reported by the OS.

InferenceCaps.description:
Inference precision capabilities.

Pre-spawn values (`capabilities_source = DeviceTable` or `Fallback`) are HINTS
only — they exist so the scheduler can make a provisional VRAM/dtype guess before
any worker has started. They are never trusted as ground truth for an actual
inference decision. The authoritative values come from the Python worker's own
runtime probe at `Ready` (`capabilities_source = PyTorch`) — see §6.6.

Job.description:
A single generation job submitted to the AnvilML scheduler.

A `Job` represents a request to run a computation graph on a worker.
It carries the graph definition, execution settings, lifecycle timestamps,
and the current status. Fields that are only populated after the job
enters a later lifecycle stage (`started_at`, `completed_at`, `worker_id`,
`error`, `queue_position`) are `Option` types.

completed_at.description: Timestamp when the job finished (completed or failed). None while running.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the job was first created and queued.

error.description: Error message if the job failed. Set only for `Failed` jobs.

graph.description: The computation graph to execute, in the format expected by workers.

id.description: Stable unique identifier for this job (UUID v4).

queue_position.description: Position in the queue. Set when `Queued`, cleared when picked up.

started_at.description: Timestamp when a worker began executing the job. None while queued.

worker_id.description: ID of the worker that executed this job. Set after execution begins.

JobSettings.description: Optional settings that control how a job is executed.

device_preference.description: Requested device. None = auto-select by VRAM.

JobStatus.description:
The lifecycle status of a generation job.

Jobs progress through this state machine:
`Queued` → `Running` → (`Completed` | `Failed`) | `Cancelled` (at any point).

ListArtifactsParams.description:
Query parameters for `GET /v1/artifacts`.

All fields are optional:
- `job_id` filters artifacts to those produced by a specific job.

job_id.description:
Optional job UUID to filter artifacts — only artifacts from this job are returned.
`None` returns all artifacts regardless of job.

ListJobsParams.description:
Query parameters for `GET /v1/jobs` (list endpoint).

All fields are optional:
- `status` filters jobs by their lifecycle status.
- `limit` caps the number of returned jobs.
- `before` is a cursor for future pagination support; the persistence
  layer does not yet use it, so it is accepted at the HTTP layer but
  silently ignored (forward-compatibility per `ANVILML_DESIGN.md §13.4`).

before.description:
Cursor for future pagination — accepted but not yet passed to the
persistence layer (forward-compatibility per `ANVILML_DESIGN.md §13.4`).
This field is intentionally unused by the handler — the struct field
exists so the HTTP API accepts the query parameter without returning
a 400 error, but the handler does not forward it to `list_jobs()`.
Stored as String because serde_urlencoded cannot deserialize
DateTime<Utc> from query strings.

limit.description: Optional maximum number of jobs to return.

oneOf.description: Optional status filter — only jobs matching this status are returned.

ListModelsParams.description:
Query parameters for the `GET /v1/models` list endpoint.

All fields are optional — when absent, the handler returns all models.

oneOf.description:
Filter results to only models of this kind.

When `None`, all models are returned regardless of kind.

ModelDtype.description:
The data type or precision of a model's weights.

This enum covers the most common weight precisions encountered in
generative-AI model files, from full FP32 through FP4 quantisation.

ModelFormat.description:
The storage format of a model file.

Each variant names a file format used to serialise model weights
on disk. The `Unknown` variant is used when the file extension or
header does not match any recognised format.

ModelKind.description:
The architecture family of a model file.

Each variant names a distinct role a model plays in the AnvilML
computation graph — diffusion base model, text encoder, VAE, LoRA
adapter, ControlNet, or upscaler.

ModelMeta.description:
Metadata about a discovered model file.

This struct is the primary output of the model scanner: it captures
the stable identity, location, architecture family, data type, file
format, size, modification time, and scan timestamp of a single
model file on disk.

id.description: Stable identifier: SHA256 hex of the first 1 MiB of the file.

mtime_unix.description: File modification time as Unix epoch seconds (populated by the scanner).

path.description: Filesystem path to the model file.

scanned_at.description: Timestamp when this metadata was scanned.

NodeTypeDescriptor.description:
Description of a node type as reported by the Python worker at Ready.

A `NodeTypeDescriptor` captures the shape of a node: its unique
identifier, human-facing metadata, and the typed input/output slots
that the scheduler uses to validate graph connectivity.

category.description: The node's category in the UI (e.g. "loaders", "conditioning").

description.description: A human-readable description of what this node does.

type_name.description: Unique identifier for this node type (e.g. "LoadModel").

ProvisioningState.description:
The provisioning status of a worker's environment.

Used by the provisioning subsystem to track whether a worker's Python
dependencies (torch, node packages) have been installed and are ready.

RemovedCount.description:
HTTP response body for `DELETE /v1/jobs` on success.

Per `ANVILML_DESIGN.md §13.4`: `200 { removed: u32 }`.

removed.description: Number of jobs removed by the bulk clear operation.

SlotDescriptor.description:
Describes one input or output slot on a node type.

Each `SlotDescriptor` defines a slot's name, semantic type, and
whether it may be omitted. Optional slots enable a node to use
an internal default when the caller does not provide a value.

name.description: The slot's identifier within the node type (e.g. "positive").

optional.description: True if this input can be omitted in favor of a node-internal default.

slot_type.description: The semantic type this slot carries.

SlotType.description:
The semantic type of a node slot.

Used by the scheduler to verify connected slots are type-compatible
at job submission time. `SlotType::Any` disables type checking for
that slot entirely, allowing any connection.

SubmitJobRequest.description:
HTTP request body for `POST /v1/jobs`.

Contains the computation graph (`serde_json::Value`) and execution
settings (`JobSettings`). The graph is validated by the scheduler
before acceptance.

graph.description: The computation graph to execute, in the format expected by workers.

SubmitJobResponse.description:
HTTP response body for `POST /v1/jobs` on success.

Per `ANVILML_DESIGN.md §13.5`: `202 { job_id, queue_position }`.

job_id.description: The UUID v4 assigned to the newly submitted job.

queue_position.description:
The job's 1-based position in the submission queue at the time of
acceptance. This is captured atomically with the enqueue operation
inside `JobScheduler::submit()`.

WorkerInfo.description:
Metadata the scheduler uses for worker selection and job assignment.

Constructed from the hardware snapshot (for `device_type`) and the worker's
registration message (for `worker_id`, `status`, `device_index`, `pid`).
The `current_job_id` is updated when the scheduler assigns a job.

current_job_id.description: The job currently assigned to this worker, if any.

device_index.description: Zero-based device index as reported by the OS/driver.

device_type.description: The compute backend of the worker's device.

pid.description: OS process ID of the worker subprocess, if known.

status.description: Current lifecycle state of the worker process.

worker_id.description: Stable worker identity — the bare device index as a string (e.g. `"0"`).

WorkerStatus.description:
The lifecycle state of a Python worker process.

Workers transition through these states as the scheduler spawns, assigns jobs,
and eventually shuts them down. The scheduler uses this enum to decide which
workers are eligible for job assignment.

State machine (per `ANVILML_DESIGN.md §5.7`):
```text
Initializing → Idle ↔ Busy → Dying → Dead → Respawning → Initializing
```
